$comment: Request/response JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12) for classifier.postman_collection.json, rendered into its items' descriptions and API_SCHEMAS.md (linked from API.md). Edit here, then: uv run --no-sync python scripts/api_schemas.py render. A schema whose $comment says `generated from …` is rewritten by unit-tests/classifier/test_api_schemas.py (API_SCHEMAS_UPDATE=1): never edit one — the JSON request models (AssessRequest, ReferenceRequest, ReferencePatch), CriterionInput, the jobs models, each criterion type's `detail` (its ResultSpec, and the stable-keys variant a `mean` aggregate keeps) and each OpenCV detector's `measurements` (its DetectorSpec). The rest is hand-written from main.py, api/*.py, analysis/pipeline.py, regions/artifacts.py, llm/usage.py and common.jobs; that test validates real output against it (analysis.analyze_document with a scripted model, the artifact routes, the introspection routes). Every error is the generic `{"detail": "<message>"}`.

CriterionInput.description:
One criterion: shared fields at the top, type-specific ones in options.

``options`` arrives as a plain object and is replaced, during validation,
by the options model for ``type`` — so every consumer reads
``c.options.hint`` on an ``llm`` criterion and never a dict.

name.description: The criterion to evaluate; unique within the request.
name.title: Name

key.description: Optional label used ONLY to find reference examples: the criterion is guided by the reference criteria with the same key (case-insensitive), whatever either is named, and never falls back to its name. options.reference.criterion wins over it. Never shown to the model; results, depends_on and prompts stay on `name`. May repeat in a request; unique within one reference.
key.title: Key

type.description: 'llm': the vision model scores it (one call per criterion). 'text': deterministic search of the text layer. 'cv': a registered OpenCV detector by name (GET /cv-detectors), with options.fallback when none matches. 'detector': the open-vocabulary detector service, using the name as its text prompt.
type.title: Type

weight.description: Relative weight in the overall score. Default 1.
weight.title: Weight

depends_on.description: Name of another SCORED criterion that must PASS first. Until it does, this criterion is not evaluated at all; if it does not, this one is SKIPPED (no model call spent). Chains propagate.
depends_on.title: Depends On

score.description: false = locate without judging: the criterion still produces regions but is excluded from the weighted score and the verdict, and its score / verdict / confidence are null. Refused for a criterion that cannot produce geometry.
score.title: Score

CriterionInput.title: CriterionInput

DocumentInput.description:
One document: base64 bytes, a URL to fetch, or inline text.

The kind (a JPEG/PNG/HEIC/HEIF/AVIF photo, PDF, SVG, .txt, .docx) is
determined from the BYTES, never from a filename or content type.
``text`` is plain text treated as a .txt
document. A URL is SSRF-checked (``common.net``) before it is fetched, at
submit time — the item cap needs the bytes (a PDF counts its pages).

type.description: 'base64': data is the file base64-encoded. 'url': data is an http(s) URL. 'text': data is the document text itself.
type.title: Type

filename.description: Recorded in document_info; never used to detect the kind.
filename.title: Filename

DocumentInput.title: DocumentInput

assess_request.description:
The whole /assess request — JSON and multipart both land here.

After validation ``documents`` is ALWAYS the list and ``document`` is
None: the single-document shorthand is normalised into a one-item list,
so nothing downstream has two shapes to handle.

documents.description: The documents, in order. Every page of every document is one item; the total is capped at CLASSIFIER_MAX_ITEMS.
documents.title: Documents

document.description: Shorthand for a one-item 'documents' list. Not with 'documents'.

criteria.description: What to evaluate. Omitted: the criteria of the listed `references`, merged by name — or, without references, the four default quality criteria.
criteria.title: Criteria

references.description: Stored worked examples (POST /references) to show the vision model beside each llm-answered criterion: a list of reference ids, "auto", or {"auto": true, "tags": [...], "tags_match": "all" | "any"}.
references.title: References

model.description: The job's model — a registry id from GET /models. Used by every llm criterion (and cv llm fallback) without its own options.model, and by the references "auto" selection call. Omitted: the registry default.
model.title: Model

job_base.$comment: generated from common.jobs.model.JobBase — do not edit
job_base.description:
Snapshot of one job at a point in time.

Fields:
    job_id: 12-char hex identifier assigned at registration.
    phase: Freeform string; each consumer defines its own convention.
        Interceptor-api uses ``"cloning" | "capturing" | "actions" |
        "cleaning_up"`` (``"actions"`` while a capture's
        ``page_script`` / ``actions`` run);
        classifier uses ``"staging" | "pending" | "processing" |
        "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled"``.
    created_at: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the job was registered.
    updated_at: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last phase / result / error
        transition. Equals ``created_at`` for a job that hasn't transitioned.
    elapsed_seconds: Wall-clock seconds since ``created_at``, computed at
        snapshot time from a monotonic clock. Present for ephemeral jobs;
        derived from ``created_at`` for persistent (SQLite-backed) jobs
        where the monotonic anchor is process-local and doesn't survive
        restarts.
    metadata: Consumer-defined dict describing the job. Typically the
        result of a pydantic ``BaseModel.model_dump()``.
    result: Populated on successful completion for persistent backends.
        Ephemeral backends never set this — a completed ephemeral job is
        already gone from the registry.
    error: Populated on failure for persistent backends. Same caveat as
        ``result`` for ephemeral.
job_base.title: JobBase

POST /v1/classifier/assess.description: Every error is the generic `{"detail": "<message>"}` -- the body is parsed by hand, so a validation failure is a 400, never FastAPI's 422: 400 every request rule (§ Request), 409 a listed reference not ready, 415 a Content-Type that is neither JSON nor multipart, 429 + `Retry-After` the queue is full (CLASSIFIER_QUEUE_LIMIT), 500 the payload could not be persisted, 502 a document URL could not be fetched.

schema.description: Each `file` / `image` part and each `text` field is one document, in form order; anything else is refused by name (a 400)

file.description: A document: JPEG, PNG, HEIC / HEIF / AVIF, PDF (any page count), SVG, .txt or .docx — repeat the part for more

text.description: An inline text document — repeat for more

criteria.description: JSON array of criterion objects (`CriterionInput`); omit to inherit the references' own

references.description: JSON array of reference ids, the word `auto`, or a JSON `{"auto": true, …}`

model.description: The job's model: a registry id from GET /models (default: the registry's)

GET /v1/classifier/jobs/:jobId.description: `?wait=<s>` holds the request until the job is completed / failed / cancelled (clamped to 60 s; a negative or non-finite one is FastAPI's 422). 404 no such job.

GET /v1/classifier/jobs/:jobId/progress.description: 404 no such job (its history went with it).

schema.description: The snapshot plus a page of the job's checkpoint history (`common.jobs.router.build_progress_router`)

attempt.description: Which run's history (null: no history yet)

events.description: A page of the history, oldest first

POST /v1/classifier/jobs/:jobId/cancel.description: 404 no such job; 409 it had already ended (`already_completed` / `already_failed` / `already_cancelled`).

DELETE /v1/classifier/jobs/:jobId.description: Deletes the row, its artifact directory, its model-usage rows and its progress history; a running job stops like a cancel. 404 no such job.

POST /v1/classifier/references.$comment: The invalid example sends {{invoice_native_b64}}, empty until it is filled in: an empty `data` is refused, as the service refuses it with a 400.
invalid_examples: References / POST /references — JSON, a document page
POST /v1/classifier/references.description: Queues the creation job. Every error is the generic body (parsed by hand): 400 a request rule, 404 / 409 / 410 a `from_job` that is unknown / not completed / swept, 409 CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_MAX_COUNT reached, 415 another Content-Type, 429 the queue is full.

schema.description: The JSON body's fields as form values; anything else is refused by name (a 400)

file.description: The ONE example page: a JPEG / PNG / HEIC / HEIF / AVIF photo, an SVG, or a PDF with `page`

criteria.description: JSON array: the same CriterionInput list /assess takes

breakdown.description: JSON object: criterion name → {score, verdict?, reason?}

tags.description: Repeat the field, or one JSON array

GET /v1/classifier/references.description: Newest first. 400 an unknown `status`; FastAPI's 422 a `limit` / `offset` out of range.

200.description: The file, typed by its name: record.json `application/json`, the page and composites `image/jpeg` / `image/png`

PATCH /v1/classifier/references/:referen.description: Only `title`, `description`, `tags` and `criteria_keys` are editable. 400 an invalid patch (parsed by hand); 404 no such reference; 409 a `criteria_keys` edit the record refuses.

schema.$comment: generated from api.reference_schemas.ReferencePatch — do not edit
schema.description:
PATCH /references/{id}: the metadata, and the criteria's keys.

An explicit null clears a title or description. ``criteria_keys`` maps a
criterion name to its new key (null clears it): a key changes how the
reference is FOUND, not what it teaches, so it sits with the lookup
metadata — and a reference saved before keys can be keyed without being
re-created. Everything else (the criteria themselves, answers, regions,
page) is immutable — a new answer key is a new reference. Here only the
key grammar is checked (``api.schemas.clean_key`` and the length cap);
that each name is a criterion, that the reference is ready and that its
keys stay unique need the record — ``api.references.patch_reference``.

tags.description: Lowercased; filter GET /references and `auto` by them.
tags.title: Tags

criteria_keys.description: {criterion name: key | null} — set (or, with null, clear) each named criterion's reference-matching key. Ready references only; keys stay unique within the reference.
criteria_keys.title: Criteria Keys

schema.title: ReferencePatch

DELETE /v1/classifier/references/:refere.description: 404 no such reference; 409 a queued or running job reads it.

GET /v1/classifier/jobs/:jobId/artifacts.description: `?criterion=<slug>` (repeatable) scopes it and adds `layers` and `filter`. 400 an unknown slug, 404 an unknown or unfinished job, 410 its directory was swept.

Rendered on first fetch when it is a layer. `criterion` / `source` / `attempt` / `accepted` filter regions.json and the combined layers. 400 an unknown slug or a filter on a name that is not a layer, 404 an unknown or unfinished job or a missing file, 410 its directory was swept.

200.description: The file, typed by its name: `.json` (regions.json, manifest.json, text.*.json) `application/json`, `.svg` `image/svg+xml`, `.png` `image/png`, `.jpg` `image/jpeg`, `text.*.txt` (the text a criterion searched) `text/plain`

GET /v1/classifier/jobs/:jobId/artifacts.description: `?criterion=<slug>` (repeatable) zips only those criteria's files. 400 an unknown slug, 404 an unknown or unfinished job, 410 its directory was swept.

200.description: Every file on disk, streamed; `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<job_id>-artifacts.zip"`

DELETE /v1/classifier/jobs/:jobId/artifa.description: Removes the directory; the job row stays. 404 an unknown job, or one with no directory.

GET /v1/classifier/jobs/:jobId/usage.description: The calls outlive the job (only DELETE /jobs/:jobId removes them). 404 neither the job nor any call is known.

anyOf.description: The response's `usage` block as the model sent it

model_id.description: The registry id (null on rows written before the registry)

calls.description: Every call, in the order made
